summary.title: RynnWorld-4D: 4D Embodied World Models for Robotic Manipulation

details: 2D pixel video world models lack geometric grounding (no depth-aware interaction, unstable object scale), while explicit 3D/4D representations (NeRF/3DGS, dynamic SfM) are scene-specific, need multi-view input, or cannot generate futures, so neither yields a scalable representation close to a robot's action space.

RynnWorld-4D: a video-diffusion world model that, from a single RGB-D frame plus a language instruction, co-generates synchronized future RGB, depth, and optical-flow videos ('projective 4D' RGB-DF) inside one shared denoising loop, with depth+flow back-projectable into metric 3D scene flow.

Architecture crux: the pretrained single-branch DiT is expanded into three modality-specific branches coupled by Joint Cross-Modal Attention modules (shared K/V per branch, frame-wise mask, 3D RoPE, zero-init output projection with learnable tanh gate) so appearance, geometry, and motion evolve consistently.

RynnWorld-4D-Policy: an inverse-dynamics head that reads the frozen world model's internal tri-branch latents in a single forward pass (no iterative denoising of video) and outputs action chunks for closed-loop control.
254.4M frames from egocentric human video (Epic-Kitchens, EgoVid) and robot manipulation corpora (RoboMIND, RDT-1B, Galaxea, RoboCoin, AgiBot).
Pseudo-labels: Qwen3-VL captions (5s clips), DPFlow optical flow (color-coded, 25 FPS), Depth Anything 3 depth clipped to [0,5] m and 8-bit quantized.
Plus 2,400 in-house teleoperated real-robot demos for world-model training and 200 episodes/task (1,200 total) for the policy.
Backbone: Wan 2.2-TI2V-5B, 30-layer DiT (d=3072); depth/flow branches initialized by duplicating pretrained weights; text cross-attention K/V shared; 10 JA modules inserted every 3 layers.

Stage 1 modality adaptation (branches independent, lr 2e-5, lambda_flow 0.5); Stage 2 frozen backbone, train only JA/norms/gates/modality embeddings (lr 5e-5, branch dropout p=0.2); Stage 3 full-parameter joint SFT (lr 1e-5, p=0.1).

Flow-matching objective with a single shared noise sample across modalities; first frame is clean conditioning (zero-flow for the flow branch) and excluded from loss; 81x480x640 videos (21 latent frames), bf16, AdamW, EMA 0.9999.

Frozen world model queried once at diffusion timestep t=500, hidden states from block 15 of all three branches concatenated; a Flow Former (learnable queries, frame-wise spatial cross-attention then temporal self-attention) compresses features.

Flow-matching action head with 4-step Euler sampling; 54-D actions, chunk length K=10; ~1.1 s cycle on RTX 5090 (FP8+FA3; world model = 89.5% of latency) giving ~9 Hz effective control with chunking, low-level interface at 500 Hz.
Hardware: dual TIANJI M6 7-DOF arms with 20-DOF WUJI dexterous hands, RealSense D435i egocentric camera; teleoperation via HTC Vive trackers + Manus gloves.

World modeling: 50 held-out sequences from RoboMIND/RDT-1B/Galaxea; metrics = PAI-Bench visual quality (IQ, MS, SC, I2V-Subject), fidelity (PSNR/SSIM/LPIPS), depth (AbsRel, delta_1<1.25 after median scaling), flow (AEPE in normalized color space).
Generation baselines: CogVideoX, Wan-2.2-TI2V-5B, Wan-2.1-I2V-14B; 4D baselines: Free4D, TesserAct (RGB-D-Normal), 4DNeX.

Real-world: success rate over 35 trials/task (120 s limit) with randomized object 6-DoF poses on six bimanual tasks (dual picking, block pushing, hand-over, bimanual lifting, lid placement, bowl stacking); policy baselines Diffusion Policy, pi_0, pi_0.5.
World model: independent (non-fused) branches, no Stage-1 modality adaptation, no large-scale 4D pretraining (task data only), no 3D RoPE in JA, shared FFN across branches.
Policy: replacing RynnWorld-4D features with a ResNet-18 encoder, and modality subsets (RGB, RGB+Depth, RGB+Flow vs. full RGB-DF).

key_findings.finding: Jointly generating RGB, depth, and flow yields substantially better geometry and the only explicit motion field among 4D world models, while matching video models on perceptual quality.
key_findings.evidence: On the held-out set RynnWorld-4D reaches delta_1 = 0.610 and AbsRel = 0.310 vs 4DNeX (0.327 / 0.423) and TesserAct (0.279 / 0.699), plus AEPE = 0.170 (baselines produce no flow); it also leads SSIM 0.754, PSNR 17.85, LPIPS 0.269, SC 0.957, while IQ (0.635) stays close to Wan-2.1-I2V-14B's 0.684.

key_findings.finding: Consuming the world model's internal 4D latents produces state-of-the-art real-world dexterous bimanual policies, with the largest gains on spatially/temporally demanding tasks.
key_findings.evidence: Success rates: Hand-over 28.57% vs DP 17.14%, pi_0 2.86%, pi_0.5 0.00%; Lid Placement and Bowl Stacking both 65.71% vs best baseline 57.14% (DP); also best on Bimanual Lifting (97.14%) and tied-best Dual Picking (94.29%).

key_findings.finding: Cross-modal fusion, not just multi-modal output, is what drives physical fidelity; modality-specific capacity and a phased curriculum are prerequisites.
key_findings.evidence: Independent branches degrade AbsRel 0.310->0.737 and AEPE 0.170->0.247; skipping Stage-1 modality adaptation drops delta_1 to 0.479; sharing one FFN across branches gives AbsRel 0.580 / delta_1 0.380 / AEPE 0.280; removing 3D RoPE inside Joint Attention drops delta_1 to 0.450 and raises AEPE to 0.210.

key_findings.finding: Predictive 4D latents are essential for the policy, and each modality contributes complementarily.
key_findings.evidence: Replacing the world-model encoder with ResNet-18 drops Dual Picking from 94.29% to 71.43% (and lowers all tasks); RGB-only latents give 77.14% Dual Picking / 14.29% Hand-over, adding depth raises Hand-over to 28.57% and Bimanual Lifting to 97.14%, adding flow helps motion-sensitive tasks, and the full RGB-DF combination is best overall.

key_findings.finding: Large-scale heterogeneous 4D pretraining is necessary; task-specific robot data alone cannot learn the dynamics.
key_findings.evidence: The w/o 4D pretraining variant collapses across axes, with AEPE rising from 0.170 to 0.729, AbsRel to 0.797, delta_1 down to 0.263, and SC down to 0.879.
